head: 89e14c4478eeb550f5c4c8438ce683f6001b6afa
claim: an app can start one local, token-protected NATS JetStream server from a hash-checked pinned download, publish to a durable stream and read it with explicit acks, and shut down without a hung process

steps: start the server with ensureNats and check health
publish a message twice with one id
read it with a durable reader that naks once then acks
close the bus, start ensureNats again on the same folder and read only the unacked message
close a bus holding a reader whose handler never settles, then stop the server
steps.result: the second start adopts the same server, only the unacked message arrives, close returns in about 5 s, and health is false after stop

verdicts.seen: Read 7 capture lines plus EXIT. Start: 'started true nats://127.0.0.1:45573 health true' with a store path. Publish/replay: 'duplicate true' (dedupe) and 'seen [["one",1],["one",2]]'. Resume: 'only unacked ["two"]' shows explicit acks. Shutdown: 'close returned in ms 5004', 'stop: health false', 'EXIT=0'. The 5004 ms close is slowish but returned and the process exited cleanly, so no hang. Token protection and hash-checked download are not shown here, but other captures can cover those. Nothing contradicts the outcome.
